The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.20.12) found new features shipping in Firefox 158 beta which was released last week. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Nightly/behind flags, it is not considered here. If a feature is missing, one reason can be that the IDL is not yet in a specification or in webref.

Firefox 158 stable releases on October 13, 2026. This PR needs to be merged before/with the BCD release on October 8, 2026.

With this PR, BCD will consider the following features as shipping in Firefox 158:

  • api.Notification.navigate
  • api.PerformanceResourceTiming.deliveryType
  • api.Sanitizer.setJavascriptURLs (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2068934)
  • api.WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly_static (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007783)
  • css.types.calc.typed_division_produces_unitless_number
  • css.types.sign.typed_division_produces_unitless_number
  • webdriver.bidi.browsingContext.captureScreenshot.imageSize_parameter
  • webdriver.bidi.browsingContext.startScreencast.destinationFolder_parameter

See also https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/158.0beta/releasenotes/

items.content_html:
Summary

• Add the missing display-capture permission descriptor to api/Permissions.json.
• Mirror browser support and status metadata from the existing api/MediaDevices.json (getDisplayMedia()) entry.

Test results and supporting details

• Defined in the W3C Screen Capture specification under Permissions Integration ("The Screen Capture API is a powerful feature that is identified by the name display-capture").
• Defined in Blink's third_party/blink/renderer/modules/permissions/permission_descriptor.idl.
• Defined in WebKit's Source/WebCore/Modules/permissions/PermissionName.idl.
• Verified runtime querying behavior in Chromium (navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'display-capture' }) returns a valid PermissionStatus).
• All schema validation, linting, and unit tests (npm run fix && npm test) passed locally with zero errors.

Related issues

Addresses the display-capture checklist item in #24831.
items.title: Add display-capture permission compatibility data

items.content_html:
Fixes #21132

Description

ScreenOrientation.lock() and unlock() are not supported in Android WebView (they are not exposed on screen.orientation in modern WebView, and were never supported or functional). They previously mirrored chrome_android.

This PR sets webview_android.version_added: false for api.ScreenOrientation.lock and api.ScreenOrientation.unlock.
items.title: ScreenOrientation: Mark lock and unlock as unsupported on Android WebView

items.content_html:
Fixes #22988

Description

In @counter-style/symbols, WebKit initially gated <image> symbol support behind an experimental flag and did not ship it enabled in Safari 17+. Like Chrome and Firefox, Safari does not support <image> values in the symbols descriptor.

This PR marks Safari's support as partial_implementation: true with an explanatory note:
Does not support \` as a value for the `symbols` descriptor.`
items.title: counter-style.symbols: Mark Safari support as partial for image values

items.content_html:
Summary

Document that before Firefox 149, URLPattern did not support lookahead and lookbehind regex syntax.

Test results and supporting details

  • In Firefox versions prior to 149, URLPattern used the Rust regex engine which did not support lookahead and lookbehind assertions, causing patterns containing them to throw. In Firefox 149 (via bug 1984171), the implementation was updated to use SpiderMonkey regex for full web compatibility.
  • Bugzilla bug 1998871: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1998871
  • Bugzilla bug 1984171: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1984171
  • Per recommendation from maintainer in #29092.

Related issues

Fixes #29092
items.title: URLPattern: Note lookahead/lookbehind regex limitations in Firefox <149

items.content_html:
dialog: Add touch dismissal bug notes for closedby in Chrome and Firefox

Fixes #30474

Description

This PR adds bug notes to html.elements.dialog.closedby regarding a touch-dismissal bug where tapping the backdrop dismisses the dialog while propagating click events to interactive elements behind the backdrop:

  • Chrome: Tapping backdrop caused click-through before Chrome 154 (Chromium issue 425579196). Fixed in Chrome 154 (ChromeStatus 6209615938322432).
  • Firefox: Tapping backdrop dismisses the dialog while triggering a click on elements behind the backdrop (Bugzilla 2022750).

Per maintainer feedback in #30474, this behavior is documented in release/support notes rather than marking partial implementation.

Motivation

Document known browser behavior and bug tracking for developers using closedby with touch interaction.
items.title: dialog: Add touch dismissal bug notes for closedby in Chrome and Firefox
